inputs.original_text: More tenancies mean little if people are still ending up in emergency accommodation and families are worried about eviction. Micheál Martin can point to lease figures, but security is what matters. Forcing landlords into six-year leases from March 1 may sound compassionate, yet piling on rules risks driving ordinary providers out and leaving renters with fewer options. Government should focus on stable homes for families, not headline numbers and policies that make the housing market harder to navigate.
inputs.modified_text: The real issue isn’t that renters have too many protections; it’s that families are still facing eviction and emergency accommodation while secure housing remains out of reach. Six-year leases from March 1 should be judged by whether they give tenants more stability, not dismissed because they might inconvenience landlords. Pointing to tenancy figures means little if people still cannot count on keeping a home. The government needs to put secure, affordable homes ahead of protecting the market’s convenience—and stop treating housing insecurity as a problem renters should simply navigate.
